do_not_assume: A family address is a Named Location.
A room needs a street address.
Creating the room makes it available to check-in.
A soft threshold and absolute threshold behave the same way.
goal: Named Locations represent the intended campus, building and room structure.
steps: Inventory the operational hierarchy and the rooms that will participate in check-in.
Open Named Locations.
Confirm or create the top-level campus location.
Add buildings beneath the campus.
Add rooms beneath the appropriate buildings.
Assign the correct Location Type to each record.
Review parent relationships and names from the full tree.
Configure only the metadata required for each location, such as thresholds, printer, beacon, point or geo-fence.
Save and verify that the hierarchy reloads correctly.
title: Recipe: Build A Check-In Location Hierarchy

decision_order: Reproduce the exact person, device, check-in configuration, campus, and Rock time.
Prove the room, group, and group-location-schedule chain is active and complete.
Prove the current schedule and device scope include that chain.
Evaluate person eligibility and room capacity against the same attempt.
Trace location-selection and workflow filters in execution order; stop at the first removal.
Check version-specific behavior only after current data and filter state are known.
do_not_assume: A room with the right name is linked to the intended group or schedule.
An active Location is open for Check-In or visible to the current device.
A schedule is active now merely because it exists on the group.
A full room, eligibility failure, or workflow filter is the cause until the same attempt proves it.
The last configured filter caused the removal; identify the first input-to-output transition.
goal: Identify the first configuration, schedule, device, capacity, eligibility, or workflow filter that removes a specific room for a specific person and check-in attempt.
read_only_checks: Read the Location record and parent path; record IsActive and any Check-In Manager open or closed state.
Read the GroupLocation joining the expected Group and Location; confirm the link is not inferred from matching names.
Read the schedule configuration on that GroupLocation and compare it with the current date and time.
Read the Device location scope and check-in configuration used by the failing kiosk or workflow.
Evaluate age, grade, ability, requirements, group membership, capacity threshold, and overflow rules for the exact person without changing them.
Inspect the workflow action log or equivalent diagnostic state and record which filter first excluded the location.
steps: Record the exact check-in configuration, person, device, campus, occurrence, and current Rock time for one reproducible attempt.
Confirm the expected Location is active, open, and under the intended campus and building hierarchy.
Confirm the expected Group is active and included by the selected check-in configuration.
Confirm a GroupLocation record joins that exact Group and Location.
Confirm the GroupLocation schedule configuration includes the intended Schedule and occurrence.
Confirm the Schedule is active at the recorded Rock time, including start date, end date, weekly time, and exclusions.
Confirm the Device and kiosk configuration are allowed to display the expected location path.
Evaluate the person's age, grade, ability, requirements, group membership, and other eligibility rules for that occurrence.
Evaluate hard or soft capacity, room-closed state, overflow behavior, and location-selection strategy.
Trace Check-In workflow filters in configured execution order and capture the first filter whose input contains the room but whose output does not.
Compare the observed filter behavior with the cited Rock source and release caveats for the installed version.
Report the first proven exclusion, the supporting record IDs or public model references, and the smallest safe configuration correction; do not change production during diagnosis.
title: Recipe: Prove Why A Check-In Room Is Not Available

do_not_assume: The special event uses every regular-service room.
The clone copies unrelated event, reservation or calendar records.
A destination schedule is safe merely because the operation completed.
goal: A destination schedule starts with the source schedule’s enabled locations.
steps: Create or identify the destination schedule.
Open the applicable check-in configuration’s Schedule view.
Choose **Clone Schedule**.
Select the existing source schedule.
Select the destination schedule.
Complete the clone.
Review every enabled location in the destination.
Remove or add only the differences required for the special event.
Test the destination schedule through the intended kiosk configuration.
Confirm that the schedule is active.
Confirm it represents the intended check-in time and category.
Confirm the check-in configuration and screen are the expected generation for the installed version.
Confirm the schedule has the required check-in timing configuration.
Confirm filters on the Schedule Builder or kiosk screen are not hiding it.
title: Recipe: Clone A Check-In Schedule For A Special Event

do_not_assume: Enabling scheduling creates assignments.
Auto Accept safely changes the state or actions of already-pending communications.
Selecting an SMS communication guarantees delivery.
goal: Groups of the selected type can schedule volunteers with defined confirmation and reminder behavior.
steps: Confirm the required Named Locations and one-schedule-per-time definitions.
Open the target Group Type’s scheduling settings.
Enable scheduling.
Select the confirmation communication.
Select the reminder communication.
Set confirmation and reminder offsets.
Choose **Ask** or **Auto Accept** deliberately.
Configure decline reasons, cancellation workflow and coordinator notifications as required.
Confirm SMS prerequisites if either communication may use SMS.
Test with a non-production assignment before broad use.
title: Recipe: Configure A Group Type For Volunteer Scheduling

do_not_assume: A preference guarantees assignment.
No location preference means the person cannot be scheduled.
A schedule template applies correctly to every weekday.
goal: A volunteer has usable availability, reminder and assignment preferences.
steps: Open the Schedule Toolbox for the correct person.
Record unavailable date ranges, scope and optional notes.
Select the applicable schedule template.
Set reminder preference.
Select preferred schedules and locations.
Confirm required Named Schedules are marked **Show Publicly** if they should appear.
Review the Group Member Detail record where administrative confirmation is needed.
Run Auto-Schedule only after preferences for the relevant roster have been reviewed.
Review generated assignments before sending confirmations.
Confirm the assignment and its schedule time.
Confirm the Group Type reminder communication and offset.
Check the group member’s reminder and communication preferences.
If no group member communication preference exists, inspect the person’s profile preference.
For SMS, confirm the provider configuration, SMS-enabled phone and SMS-capable System Communication.
For Outreach Toolbox, separately inspect the reminder job time and push delivery in the target mobile environment.
title: Recipe: Prepare Volunteer Availability For Auto-Schedule

do_not_assume: A calendar feed bypasses Rock security.
A volunteer Schedule Toolbox link is the same as an Event Calendar feed.
A reservation automatically appears on the event calendar.
goal: The intended Rock calendar is available through a bounded iCalendar feed.
steps: Confirm the event, occurrences, active state, calendars and approval state.
Open the intended Event Calendar.
use **Export Calendar Feed** to obtain the URL.
Review its calendar, campus, audience and date parameters.
Confirm the requesting user can access any non-public calendar included.
Subscribe from a test calendar client.
Compare representative occurrences, dates and descriptions with Rock.
Retest after changing one test occurrence.
Document the feed’s audience and ownership.
Confirm the Room Management plugin is installed and identify its version.
Identify the reservation and its explicit calendar linkage.
Compare schedule, location and contact fields without modifying either record.
Determine which record is authoritative under local policy.
Review the recipe generation and schema assumptions before running a workflow or SQL.
Stop before synchronizing if ownership, linkage or compatibility is ambiguous.
title: Recipe: Publish And Test An Event Calendar Feed

do_not_assume: Rock core synchronizes reservations and calendars.
An older custom attribute and a newer linkage table are interchangeable.
A recipe’s embedded IDs, paths or table names apply locally.
A mismatch tells the agent which record should win.
goal: The organization has a safe compatibility and ownership decision before implementing synchronization.
steps: Confirm whether the Room Management plugin is installed.
Record its exact version and linkage schema.
Identify the community recipe that matches that generation.
Determine whether reservations or calendar occurrences are authoritative for schedule, location and contact fields.
Inspect existing reservation linkages and mismatches read-only.
Review all proposed Lava, workflow actions, SQL, routes and permissions.
Test in a non-production environment with reversible sample records.
Verify create, update, missing-link and mismatch cases.
Approve a production workflow only after security, performance and rollback review.

do_not_assume: Pre-v19 systems have the same materialization.
The supplied evidence defines the generation horizon or refresh mechanism.
One organization’s observed row count is universal.
On pre-v19 systems, do not assume the v19 materialization model exists.
goal: A date-based report uses Rock’s v19 materialized schedule occurrences.
steps: Confirm the installed version is v19.
Identify the recurring Schedule records in scope.
Inspect their corresponding `ScheduleDate` rows.
Compare representative generated dates with the intended recurrence.
Update the report design to filter and join through generated dates.
Test inclusions, exclusions and date boundaries.
Stop rather than adding a parallel recurrence parser when generated dates are unexpectedly absent.
Confirm the installed Rock version.
On v19, inspect the generated `ScheduleDate` rows for the schedule.
Use those rows for date-based SQL or Lava rather than re-expanding the iCalendar rule.
If expected rows are absent, stop and verify generation behavior for the exact installed build.
On pre-v19 systems, do not assume the v19 materialization model exists.
title: Recipe: Audit A V19 Date-Based Schedule Query
